clue.text: Politicians found in work gang?

parts.note: labour means work, toil
a party is a group or gang of people, as in a search party

explanation.surface: A question whether a group of manual workers counts as a bunch of politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour Party is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party is a British political party, so its members are a body of politicians.

clue.text: The last word in steam engines

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words steam engines

explanation.surface: A claim that some locomotive is the ultimate in steam power.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing word of a prayer or hymn is this one, so it is literally the final word said.

clue.text: Player's award covering second position in podium

indicators.note: covering means the award's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: second position in picks the letter standing second in the word podium

explanation.surface: A competitor's medal is draped over the runner-up spot on the winners' podium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts O, the second letter of 'podium', inside OBE. 'Player' is a musical instrument, one who plays in the orchestra by metonymy.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument, or the musician playing it in an orchestra, is a player.

clue.text: Study that is primarily seeking money

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word seeking is used

explanation.surface: Advice that learning is mostly about chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: READIES is British slang for ready cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is informal British slang for cash in hand, banknotes ready to spend.

clue.text: A kiss is forming an alliance

parts.note: X is the cross written for a kiss at the end of a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A romantic peck seals a partnership between two people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the Second World War alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan; the word means such a pact between states.

clue.text: Most of them charge? Yes, for treatment

indicators.note: most of means the word them loses its last letter

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in to beat the rap
Y stands for yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether those people bill for their services and is told they do, for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last letter of 'them' to leave THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological treatment given to heal a disorder.

clue.text: Part of church where it's sin to go topless

indicators.note: to go topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down clue

parts.note: a lapse is a moral slip or sin

explanation.surface: A joke about a place in church where baring one's chest is sinful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' removes L from LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: 6 gets a prize — a French cruet set

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 6-down, a word for treatment

parts.note: a cup is a trophy or prize
un is French for a

indicators.note: set means the letters of cruet are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A winner receives a trophy and a French condiment set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges CRUET to CTURE. The definition is the answer to 6-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Acupuncture, inserting fine needles into the skin, is a form of alternative treatment.

clue.text: Large-scale map at last — one found in Europe

indicators.note: found in means the pieces sit within the letters for Europe

parts.note: EC, the European Community, stands for Europe

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word map

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A detailed map turns out to have one place located in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: P (end of 'map') and I go inside EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something on a grand or heroic scale, like a long narrative poem.

clue.text: Lacking spirit, soldier made off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disheartened soldier deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost confidence and morale is dispirited, lacking spirit.

clue.text: Profound river pilot's leader

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word pilot's

explanation.surface: A river pilot is praised as a wise guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep thoughts are profound ones, going far beneath the surface.

clue.text: Fire-raiser

parts.note: an arsonist on the surface, but read literally an object that holds a small flame up high

explanation.definitionFit: This holder raises a lit wax taper above the table, so it lifts fire.

clue.text: Dress down, darling — supporting vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other one

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
pet is a term of endearment, darling

explanation.surface: Someone tells a darling to wear casual clothes while propping up a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress down' is not about casual clothes: it means to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them, as one summoned to the boss's carpeted office.

clue.text: Embarrassed at a party in front of the editor

indicators.note: in front of places the earlier pieces before the next one

parts.note: a bash is an informal party
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone is red-faced at a party in front of their editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means disconcerted or ashamed, made self-conscious.

clue.text: Musicians' subs paid in time

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for pieces or pairs belonging to musicians, read loosely as musicians' works

indicators.note: in means the letter for time sits inside the other piece

parts.note: subs are membership dues paid

explanation.surface: Band members' subscriptions were paid promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Duets are compositions for two performers, works that musicians play in pairs.

clue.text: Simple box stand uncovered

parts.note: to spar is to box in practice

indicators.note: uncovered means the word stand loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: An unadorned boxing ring stands open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the first and last letters of 'stand', leaving TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and plain, like the frugal ancient Spartans.

clue.text: Broke with family, they're in the way

indicators.note: in means the family letters sit within the street letters

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Penniless relatives are getting under someone's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is informal British slang for having no money at all.

clue.text: Scoff in attempt to reach agreement

indicators.note: in means the eating word sits inside the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an effort to reach a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mockery; here it means eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations.

clue.text: In a mood for our country to be split by cunning

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'In a mood for our country to be split by cunning': UK inside SLY gives SUKLY or SLUKY, never SULKY; no parse gives the answer and no source shows the clue differently.
annotationWithheld.clue: In a mood for our country to be split by cunning

clue.text: The lowdown on opium?

definitions.meaning: the inside information on something, the gen
a drug such as opium, slang for narcotics

explanation.surface: A request for the inside story on a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang both for inside information and for drugs such as cannabis or opium.

clue.text: One side departed

definitions.meaning: the port or sinister side, opposite to right

explanation.surface: Someone from one team went away.
explanation.definitionFit: Left is both the side opposite right and the past tense of leave.

clue.text: Agreed to make reparation

definitions.meaning: read as two words, in accord or in harmony
to make amends for a wrong

explanation.surface: Parties concur that amends must be made.
explanation.definitionFit: At one means in agreement, and atone means make amends for a wrong.

clue.text: Country motorists outside working in lab

indicators.note: outside means the motorists' letters go around the rest

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motorists' organisation

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of in lab are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Drivers stand outside, toiling in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like a description of the motorists; it is the anagram signal for the two words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan nation on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Learned English, it appeared in vulgar surroundings

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, means the little word sits within the vulgar word

parts.note: rude means vulgar, coarse
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English scholar turned up in coarse company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' is the adjective, scholarly, not the past tense of learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means having great knowledge gained from study, scholarly.

clue.text: Involves being in French evening dress

parts.note: en is French for in
tails are a formal tailcoat worn in the evening

explanation.surface: A formal event requires a French tailcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: If one thing entails another, it necessarily involves or requires it.

clue.text: The Yorkshire beast is a horse that nearly runs

definitions.text: The Yorkshire beast is a horse that nearly runs

parts.words: The Yorkshire beast is a horse that nearly runs
parts.note: a description of a breed of horse whose gait is quicker than a walk but short of a gallop

explanation.definitionFit: A horse bred to move at a brisk two-beat pace, short of a run, is named for that gait.

clue.text: It's a load of rubbish, mate!

definitions.meaning: a British form of address to a man, like pal

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend he is talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh means nonsense and is also an informal British way of addressing a stranger, like chum.

clue.text: Pulls up the student who works hard

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: tows means pulls along

explanation.surface: Someone tells off the diligent student.
explanation.walkthrough: SWOT is British slang for a pupil who studies hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for a pupil who studies obsessively.

clue.text: Get the most out of this drink

explanation.surface: A promise to enjoy this beverage to the full.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk a situation is to exploit it fully; it is also the dairy drink.

clue.text: The French court is about to return the powder

indicators.note: to return means the whole assembled run is read backwards
is about means the court letters go around the French article

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: A French tribunal is about to hand back some powder.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal indicator turns the whole container, built first, not just the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine body powder.

clue.text: Nothing more than water

explanation.surface: It is just water.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means only, and a mere is also a lake or pool.

clue.text: Frightened — suggested I'd go inside!

indicators.note: go inside means those letters are put within the other word

parts.note: intimated means hinted or suggested
I'd without the apostrophe gives these two letters

explanation.surface: Someone scared hints that they would retreat indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightened' could be a plain past tense; here it means cowed, the adjective sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cowed by threats is to be frightened.

clue.text: The fool started to challenge fate

indicators.note: started to means only the start of the word challenge is used

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: An idiot began to defy destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Section of parliament that might check BSE ban

indicators.note: might signals that the letters could be formed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: MPs might oppose a ban related to mad cow disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' rearranges CHECK BSE BAN. BSE is mad cow disease; backbenchers are MPs without ministerial posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear benches of the Commons, and the MPs who sit there without office, form a part of parliament.
